_comment: user_agent: a browser User-Agent for every link checked. Sites increasingly
answer an unrecognised agent with 403 -- ivarjacobson.com is the one that
forced this, serving 403 to the default agent and 200 to a browser -- and a
403 that only a bot ever sees is not a dead link. Setting the agent is the
accurate fix: widening aliveStatusCodes to accept 403, or ignoring each
offending URL one by one, would suppress genuine breakage instead.
It must be the top-level `user_agent` key, NOT an httpHeaders entry.
link-check hands needle a `user_agent` option that defaults to
'link-check/<version>', and needle applies that over anything set through
headers -- so a User-Agent placed in httpHeaders is silently discarded and
the 403 persists. This was verified both ways.
